speaker: abel_garnish
text: Thirty-five lines in three days, and one whole song. I heard the song in the yard, not in the parlour. The pin goes in. The morning's scrap is dead. This is the thing they shouted back.

speaker: will_kemp
text: They shouted it because it was mine and because they were full of pancake and mischief. You may have the thirty-five. I had the faces. Write the faces too, if you are feeling literary. No. I see you are not.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Say the tally. I am not copying the lines into the book today. Thirty-five can be said aloud. The lines can wait until a morning that is not this one. You have the song. That is the news. I am not fair-copying a holiday.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thou art right to leave the book. The third time held. Navarre held. The yard was thick, and they were loud, and the loudness was not all pancake. I am not asking thee to improve it in the tiring-room because a prentice beat the time.

speaker: john_heminges
text: My lord's health. We drink it here, and we do not count the years at this table. The day is his. The comedy was ours. Both can be true without a sum.

speaker: will_kemp
text: His health, then. I can drink a man without weighing him. If anyone reaches for a number I will put the cup in his hand and the number back in his pocket. We are players, not a parish register.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No number. I have seen the almanac. It gives the day and the birthday, and it stops. We stop where it stops. John, your cup is the whole arithmetic I want.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Then the arithmetic is done. Stack the trestles. They are the inn's, not the company's. This was the last play in this yard before the dark. I am not leaving our boards mixed with their furniture, and I am not making a ceremony of the stacking.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Stack them. The book comes with me. Thirty-five is in my head and will be in the margin when I have a table that is not wet. It is not in the play-book tonight. Master Will said wait, and for once the wait is cheaper than the ink.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The dark begins tomorrow. Thou wilt not come to me with a midnight page, Will. We stopped cleanly enough for my lord, if cleanly means we finished the bill and did not start a quarrel in the street. I saw no stick. I am content with no stick.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No stick, and no midnight page. The King is off. The holiday is over when these boards are up. Thou hast the ending as the yard played it, Dick. I am not visiting it again tonight.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Visit the song, if you visit anything. One whole song. Abel has said it, so it exists, which is more than a scrap at nine in the morning ever did. You may thank the prentices. They were the instrument. I was merely inspired, and I mention it because no one else will.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Thank them by stacking, not by a speech. The gatherers are done. I am not calling a figure for the house in this room. The trestle under your boot is the inn's, Will Kemp. Move the boot.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The boot is moved. The modesty remains. Thirty-five is a handsome number and I shall not round it up, because Abel would cry, and I have had enough tears for one Shrove.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: They are not done, even if we are. Listen, and then do not go out and argue with a holiday. Thou hast a home. The yard has its own end. I am not policing pancake.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I hear them. I am not going out to answer. The edge is there. It can stay there. John, the trestles. Abel, the thirty-five, said and not copied. Dick, I will see thee when the house is a house again, and not tomorrow on a stage.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Said, and not copied. I will write the tally where I write tallies. I will not write the nine that are his newest into the comedy tonight. If I write them tonight I shall write them wrong, and he will tell me I have stolen his breath. Tomorrow is a church day. The book can survive a church day.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The book can survive, and the purse can survive, and the inn can have its furniture back. My lord has had his health. The Mayor has not had a stick. I call that a Tuesday. Help me with the long trestle. It is heavier than a moral.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Heavier than a moral, and less useful. Lift. I have sung, I have eaten, I have been numbered. If you need a fourth hand, take Will's. He is standing there having thoughts, and thoughts do not stack a board.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have the end of it. Thoughts can wait until the board is up. Thirty-five. One song. No age. No copy in the book. Thou canst stop reciting me, Dick. I am lifting.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Lift, then. Thirty-five is spoken. One song is spoken. The book stays shut until I have a dry table and a morning that is not Shrove. I am not giving anyone a fair copy as a pudding.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Nor a new ending as a pudding. Thou hast said no midnight page, Will. I am holding thee to it. My shoulder has done the moral work. The board is the board.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The long one is up. The short ones are the inn's as well. Leave them in their stack by the wall, not in our baskets. I will not hire a man to sort furniture we do not own.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Stacked. Numbered. Sung. Uncopied. If they are still shouting when you reach the street, do not preach at them. They have had their play. So have you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not preach. I will not copy. I am going when this last board is honestly up, and not before. Thirty-five stands where Abel said it. The book does not.
